results.title: Stark County Parcels
results.description:
This parcel polygon layer is the primary parcel layer used with Stark County, Ohio. The parcel boundaries are maintained by the Stark County Auditor Office (SCAO) Tax Map Department. The SCAO uses a Computer-Assisted mass Appraisal (CAMA) database to maintain and store data on properties throughout the county. This data includes market valuations, property owners and addresses, and a variety of other information. This layer combines the parcel boundaries and the CAMA data using a SQL view. There are a number of other layers publicly-available by the county that include other combinations of parcel boundaries and background attribute data.

For foreclosure data, see Historic Foreclosures.
For the market values of properties, see Market Values.
For historic parcel sales, see Parcel Sales.

results.title: Certified Delinquent Parcels
results.description: This mapping service shows Stark County parcels that are certified as delinquent by the Stark County Treasurer's Office. Every year the Treasurer’s office collects 1st and 2nd half taxes typically due in February and July. Due dates vary by year. Although tax payer’s properties or parcels can be marked as delinquent for late payments, the parcel will not be marked or flagged as a certified delinquent parcel until the end of a reconciliation period which ends mid- August. A parcel will remain as a certified delinquent parcel until the Balance is paid in full (In other words, the Balance is $0.00).
results.snippet: This service shows the parcels that are certified as delinquent in Stark County, OH.

results.title: Property Sales
results.description: A polygon depiction of property sales from 2010 to the present that occurred in Stark County, Ohio. The Stark County Auditor's Office (SCAO) maintains records of property sales using a Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) Database. This layer is a SQL view combining the sales records from the CAMA database with the Stark County parcel layer. A new view is created every morning through a combination of python scripts and SQL stored procedures. The data always reflects the most-recent information available from the previous day for both sources.

results.title: Housing Rehab Program - Disqualification Parcels
results.description:
Properties that are ineligible for funding under the Stark County Regional Planning Commission's (SCRPC) Housing Rehab Program (HRP). Under the HRP, residents can take advantage of different types of federal assistance to rehabilitate their home. There is a handful of criteria residents must meet to be considered eligible for any of these programs. If any one of these criteria is not met, the resident is considered ineligible. These criteria are:
  • Residents must not live in Canton, Massillon, or Hills & Dales. The program for Alliance is separate, but because it is managed by SCRPC, it is not excluded on this map.
  • Must be the owner of a single-family residence for at least one year.
  • Must qualify as low-to-moderate income.
  • Cannot owe money to a government agency and must have no unpaid judgement or liens. Must be current on mortgage payments and property taxes. Bankruptcies must be discharged.
This layer uses four separate layers to display ineligibility in order of how they are checked.
  1. The top layer, Ineligible Communities rules out the entire jurisdiction of Canton, Massillon, and Hills & Dales.
  2. The second layer, Not LUC-510 (1-Family Home) rules out any properties that are not coded as LUC-510: 1-Family Residential.
  3. The third layer, LUC-510 (1-Family Home): Transferred within Past Year rules out any single-family residence that has been transferred in the past year.
  4. The bottom layer, LUC-510 (1-Family Home): Delinquent rules out any property that is currently delinquent for their property tax or other government payment.
These layers are ranked by how many properties they exclude. The only criteria not included in this layer is whether a resident is low-to-moderate income. That information is not available in the GIS.

For more information on the SCRPC HRP, visit https://www.starkcountyohio.gov/community-development/programs/housing-rehabpublished-page?ext=..

results.title: Stark County Fee Parcels
results.description:
The Constitutions of both the United States and the State of Ohio allow the government to seize private property under eminent domain for public use. The private party is compensated fairly based on market values for the property acquisition. The features in this layer are primarily right-of-way acquisitions by the county as part of road improvement projects. Eminent domain acquisitions may less commonly occur for other purposes, such as the seizure of excess land. 

 
The attribute table provides legal information such as where and when the parcel acquisition was recorded. It also provides information on the parties involved in the acquisition, as well as information about where the parcel is located and what purpose it serves.

results.name: Bus_Routes_Index
results.title: Bus Routes Index
results.description:
Vector-tile layer of parcels symbolized by the Access to Bus Routes Index used to determine focus areas for the Microeconomic Initiative.

Strengthening Stark is an initiative spurred from the Stark Civic Group to accelerate economic growth and increase access to opportunity for all residents in Stark County, Ohio. As a starting point, Hrishue Mahalaha, the Chief Economic Development Consultant for Strengthening Stark tasked Stark County GIS (SCGIS) with analyzing specific socioeconomic and business variables to identify a few areas to focus on. We identify this task as the Microeconomic Initiative. The six variables Hrishue aimed to see and how they were derived are:

  • Job Density - The number of jobs within a quarter-mile of a parcel. These existing jobs were derived from business data obtained from the ReferenceUSA database. The businesses were geocoded and employee concentrations were created using point density analysis.

  • Access to Bus Routes - The number of different bus routes accessible to a parcel within a quarter-mile walk of a parcel. Bus routes and the bus stops they are accessible through were provided by the Stark Area Regional Transit Authority (SARTA) and are current as of mid-2019.

  • Access to Childcare - The capacity of nearby childcare facilities within a quarter-mile walk of a parcel. Childcare data was collected by Stark County Jobs and Family Services (SCJFS). Max capacity was chosen as the variable to use because it indicates the size of the childcare facilities a parent would have nearby access to.

  • Unemployment - The percentage of people unemployed out of the total workforce. This data is from the 2017 American Community Survey (ACS) at the block group level. The ACS is an annual survey conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) to provide demographic data to communities across the country.

  • Poverty - The percentage of people living below the poverty threshold. This data is from the 2017 ACS at the block group level.

  • Per-Capita Income - The per-capita income of people living within a census block group. This data is from the 2017 ACS.

results.name: Weighted_Composite_Index
results.title: Weighted Composite Index
results.description:
Vector-tile layer of parcels symbolized by the weighted composite index of 6 variables used to determine focus areas for the Microeconomic Initiative. The weighted composite index uses all 6 variables as the Composite Index does, but applies the following weights to each individual score: Job Density & Access to Bus Routes = 0.3; Access to Childcare = 0.15; Unemployment, Poverty, & Per-Capita Income = 0.0833. The highest weights were applied to Job Density & Access to Bus Routes because we believed these to be the two-most important variables. We applied equal weights to the 3 socioeconomic variables (Unemployment, Poverty, & Per-Capita Income) for a total of 0.25 to ensure these three similar variables did not weigh too heavily.

Strengthening Stark is an initiative spurred from the Stark Civic Group to accelerate economic growth and increase access to opportunity for all residents in Stark County, Ohio. As a starting point, Hrishue Mahalaha, the Chief Economic Development Consultant for Strengthening Stark tasked Stark County GIS (SCGIS) with analyzing specific socioeconomic and business variables to identify a few areas to focus on. We identify this task as the Microeconomic Initiative. The six variables Hrishue aimed to see and how they were derived are:

  • Job Density - The number of jobs within a quarter-mile of a parcel. These existing jobs were derived from business data obtained from the ReferenceUSA database. The businesses were geocoded and employee concentrations were created using point density analysis.

  • Access to Bus Routes - The number of different bus routes accessible to a parcel within a quarter-mile walk of a parcel. Bus routes and the bus stops they are accessible through were provided by the Stark Area Regional Transit Authority (SARTA) and are current as of mid-2019.

  • Access to Childcare - The capacity of nearby childcare facilities within a quarter-mile walk of a parcel. Childcare data was collected by Stark County Jobs and Family Services (SCJFS). Max capacity was chosen as the variable to use because it indicates the size of the childcare facilities a parent would have nearby access to.

  • Unemployment - The percentage of people unemployed out of the total workforce. This data is from the 2017 American Community Survey (ACS) at the block group level. The ACS is an annual survey conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) to provide demographic data to communities across the country.

  • Poverty - The percentage of people living below the poverty threshold. This data is from the 2017 ACS at the block group level.

  • Per-Capita Income - The per-capita income of people living within a census block group. This data is from the 2017 ACS.
